title.narrative: Strengthening Pacific Financial Systems and Fiscal Policy Initiative 2022-23 to 2027-28

description.narrative: The Pacific Financial Technical Assistance Centre (PFTAC) is the IMF’s capacity development arm in the Pacific. The IMF’s capacity development work, covering technical assistance and training, is one of the three core functions of the IMF, along with surveillance and lending. This work supports the efforts of Pacific IMF member countries to build the institutions and capacity necessary to formulate and implement sound economic and financial policies. The IMF’s capacity development work through PFTAC is focused on those with the greatest capacity building needs, including fragile states. Together with surveillance and lending, capacity development is a critical tool to promote economic stability and growth among IMF members.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: Assistance was provided to Palau to strengthen Public Finance Management (PFM) practices to build resilience into budget and investment policy and practices. Utilising International Monetary Fund’s (IMF’s) Green PFM framework, PFTAC introduced Green PFM practices in Palau by incorporating climate change into medium-term fiscal strategy and risk management, planning and budget decision making while incorporating climate considerations into public investment. Modalities for incorporating climate exposure and vulnerability information in fixed asset registers to ensure resilience of the infrastructure network and developing methodologies for determining appropriate levels of maintenance in response to climate related and natural disaster hazards were also developed. This work will form a template for taking Green PFM and other gender and disability related framework forward with other PFTAC member countries.

In the area of revenue policy and administration, PFTAC supports member countries to strengthen the capacities of tax administrations, mobilizing tax revenue, improving taxpayer compliance, and promoting citizens’ ownership of their role as taxpayers. PFTAC technical assistance helped Palau in its Tax Reform, including by improving efficiency in revenue mobilization, and supporting the implementation of the Palau Goods and Services Tax (PGST) system. PGST in 2024 made up 49 per cent of Palau’s tax revenue composition. PFTAC facilitated peer-to-peer learning by bringing together Palau and Marshall Islands revenue administrations to collaborate on tax reform and digital transformation. Drawing on this experience, the Palau Bureau of Revenue and Taxation will offer support to the Marshall Islands as they implement their own tax reform in FY2026.

PFTAC’s Public Finance Management (PFM) program recorded an unprecedented number of comprehensive Public Expenditure and Financial Accountability (PEFA) assessments. Three agile PEFA assessments were conducted and approved in Fiji, Tuvalu and Vanuatu. All three evaluations noted improvements compared to previous assessments, indicating progress in the implementation of reforms over the years. Notably, the assessment for Fiji showed more significant advancements across the PFM cycle. Two Climate Public Investment Management Assessments (C-PIMA) were conducted in Fiji and Papua New Guinea. Together, these assessments provide governments with the evidence base and structured guidance needed to prioritize reforms, strengthen fiscal institutions, and align national investment strategies with climate resilience and development objectives.

The PFTAC Government Finance Statistics (GFS) program leverages improvements to Financial Management Information Systems (FMIS) to deliver better quality fiscal statistics across the region. A recent example is GFS technical assistance enhancing efforts by facilitating knowledge sharing and fostering peer-to-peer learning among member countries. In Cook Islands, PFTAC developed a new template to reduce manual efforts and reviewed the national accounting practices. Peer-to-peer learning exercises held with Solomon Islands’ experts assisted in identifying improvements in GFS that lead to better quality inputs to GDP estimates. In Marshal Islands, improved mapping of GFS from a new chart of accounts led to better quality data and production of quarterly reporting. In Kiribati, PFTAC supported the introduction of a time-series analysis tool to aid data verification prior to dissemination. Further review and improvement to classification of GFS data led to the development of a financial balance sheet for the first time. The first GFS TA mission to Niue established a process to enable the authorities to compile basic GFS statements for the first time.

The PFTAC revenue program supports major tax reform processes in the region. This allows governments to understand the revenue and welfare impacts of various tax changes. PFTAC has been actively engaged in the Solomon Islands' Inland Revenue Division (IRD), offering expert guidance aimed at the comprehensive overhaul of the tax system in line with international best practice. PFTAC’s analysis and support has formed the basis of the Asian Development Bank (ADB)-led Tax Modernization Project. As part of this project, the IRD has implemented a new organizational structure to strengthen governance and compliance, upgrades to digital infrastructure, and has prioritized gender equality across all dimensions of its initiative to modernize tax administration. Efforts are also focused on improving the efficiency of the tax system through the Value-Added Tax (VAT) and changes to the Income Tax system, as well as making the tax system fairer.
